name: Savory
grown_as: Winter savory, a small, nearly evergreen shrubby perennial. Summer savory (Satureja hortensis) is an annual with softer grey leaves; the drawings have no seed stages, so winter savory is assumed. ⚠️ CHECK which William grows.
habit: A compact, low bush 20 to 40 cm high, many upright or spreading stems from a woody base.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, often with tufts of small leaves in the joints
leaf.outline: Narrow, lance-shaped to strap-shaped, 1 to 3 cm long and 2 to 5 mm wide
leaf.margin: Smooth, no teeth; fine hairs along the edge near the base
leaf.surface: Stiff, leathery, glossy, dotted with tiny glands

flower.petals: Joined; a notched upper lip and a three-lobed lower lip
flower.colour: White to pale lilac, the lower lip spotted purple
flower.behind: A green bell-shaped calyx with five pointed teeth
flower.carried: In small clusters of 3 to 7 in the joints of the upper leaves, making loose leafy spikes

fruit: Tiny brown nutlets in the dry calyces.
winter: Nearly evergreen: a twiggy bush with some dark leaves left.

leaf: a narrow leaf with a sharp point
bloom: small white to pale lilac two-lipped flowers
purple spots on the lower lip
in small clusters in the leaf joints
young: a small upright plant with narrow pointed leaves in opposite pairs
crop: a compact low bush of many stems clothed in narrow, glossy dark green leaves
flower: small white or pale lilac flowers clustered in the upper leaf joints along leafy spikes

look_alikes: Summer savory is an annual with soft, greyish, narrower leaves and pale pink flowers. Thyme has much smaller leaves and flowers in tight heads. Hyssop is bigger with violet-blue spikes.
